biography: Trevor Carmody's journey began not on a racetrack, but on the dusty backroads of rural Oklahoma, dodging tumbleweeds in his grandfather's beat-up pickup truck. That's where he learned car control, albeit unintentionally. His real racing education started at 14, tearing up the local karting scene. He quickly outgrew the karts, craving more power and a bigger challenge. A defining moment came at a regional karting championship, where he made a daring last-lap overtake, cementing his reputation as a fearless competitor. He transitioned to open-wheel racing at 17, showing flashes of brilliance mixed with youthful recklessness. Currently, at 21, Trevor is making waves in the Formula Regional Americas Championship, driving for his own self-funded 'Trevor Carmody' team, constantly battling against better-funded and more experienced rivals. He is known to be a diamond in the rough, needing some refinement, but possessing raw speed and determination.
drivingStyle: Carmody's driving style is all about aggression. He attacks every corner with the ferocity of a cornered animal, often pushing the limits of grip to the absolute maximum. His tire management is questionable at times, sacrificing early pace for a potential late-race advantage, or more often, ending up with shredded rubber. He thrives under pressure, relishing the opportunity to make daring overtakes. He is known for late braking and isn't afraid to make contact, sometimes to his detriment.

rivalries.name: Isabelle Rossi
rivalries.reason: Rossi, a seasoned veteran, publicly criticized Carmody's aggressive driving after a controversial incident at Road America, sparking a heated on-track and off-track feud.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: Tanaka represents the established order of well-funded teams that Carmody is trying to disrupt. Their rivalry is based on Carmody's desire to prove that talent can beat money.

rivalries.name: Marcus Dubois
rivalries.reason: Dubois and Carmody have been battling since their karting days. Dubois, always the technically superior driver, resents Carmody's raw speed and reckless abandon.

quirks: He always wears the same lucky wristband given to him by his grandfather before every race.
He listens to heavy metal music at full volume right before getting into the car to get pumped up.
He refuses to walk under ladders, even in the paddock area.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. If you ain't rubbing, you ain't racing."
careerHighlight: Winning the Skip Barber Racing School Scholarship Runoff in 2020, earning him a fully funded season in the Skip Barber Formula Race Series, which launched his professional career.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the last lap of the 2022 Formula Regional Americas race at VIR, throwing away a guaranteed victory and valuable championship points.
